proposals.title: Rebuild Huahua: a 30-seat active set
proposals.summary:
# Rebuild Huahua 🐕

Chihuahua is changing fast, and if you have followed the last few upgrades you have seen it:

- **v9.5.0** closed the Alliance chapter and cleaned up what was left behind.
- **v10.0.0** moved the chain to the current Cosmos stack: SDK v0.54, CometBFT v0.39, CosmWasm 3 and IBC v11. Burned fees are now counted on chain, `x/liquidity` lives in the Chihuahua repository, and the modules we no longer use are gone.
- The connection with Osmosis is back.

We are not patching an old chain anymore. We are rebuilding it into something bigger and more complete, one step at a time. This proposal is the next step, and this time it is about the people who run the network.

## The change

One staking parameter: `max_validators` goes from **80 to 30**. Everything else stays the same.

## Why

Chihuahua has 80 seats in the active set, but only **24 validators are active** today. 56 seats are empty.

With that many free seats there is no race: anyone who bonds a single HUAHUA and stays unjailed gets in, and nobody can be pushed out. A validator that misses blocks or upgrades late keeps its seat exactly like one that is always there.

80 made sense when Chihuahua had more than 80 validators fighting for a place. Today it is a ceiling nobody reaches. 30 is a number we can fill, and a full set is a set that has to earn its place.

## What 30 means

- **No active validator is removed.** 24 is below 30, the current set stays as it is.
- **The door is open.** 6 seats are free for new validators and for jailed ones ready to come back.
- **Seats are worth something again.** When more than 30 validators want in, the 30 with the most stake are active. The rest earn their way in by running a solid node, upgrading on time and showing up in governance.

There are 224 jailed validators, many still holding delegations that earn nothing. As that stake moves to active validators and new teams join, the 30 seats will fill up and the race begins. That is what we want: a set of validators that compete to be the best.

## Why not fewer

A smaller number, like 20, would push out small validators that are doing a good job today. The goal is a stronger set, not a smaller one.

## What you can do

- **Validators:** keep your node healthy and up to date. If you were thinking of joining, now is a good time.
- **Delegators:** check where your stake is. If your validator is jailed or inactive you earn nothing: redelegate to an active one, and spread your stake. More validators with real stake means a stronger chain for all of us.

The number can always be changed again by governance.

More is coming. Let's rebuild Huahua together. 🐕🔥

proposals.title: Recover expired IBC client 07-tendermint-45 (Osmosis), second attempt
proposals.summary:
Recovers the expired IBC client 07-tendermint-45 (Chihuahua's light client of osmosis-1, used by channel-7 <-> Osmosis channel-113) with the active substitute 07-tendermint-226.

Proposal 98 asked the same and passed, but its execution failed ("subject client state does not match substitute client state"): the substitute 07-tendermint-224 was created with a relayer's defaults, max_clock_drift 600s, while 07-tendermint-45 has 25s. MsgRecoverClient requires every parameter to match except height, trusting period and chain id.

07-tendermint-226 is a clone of 07-tendermint-45: identical client state, only the latest height moved to a recent osmosis-1 header (agreed by several independent RPCs) and a 9-day trusting period. It was checked against the ibc-go v8.7.0 rules, and the whole recovery was rehearsed on a fork of mainnet state: a 600s substitute fails with the same error as proposal 98, the clone passes, 07-tendermint-45 becomes Active and accepts new Osmosis headers.

After recovery a relayer refreshes the client daily so it cannot expire again.

proposals.title: Chihuahua v10.0.0 software upgrade
proposals.summary:
**Upgrade height: 25586332**, expected around 2026-10-03 14:07 UTC ([countdown](https://explorer.chihuahua.wtf/block/25586332)).

**This proposal is expedited (24-hour voting period).** For technical reasons, v10.0.0 needs to be applied sooner than the usual governance timeline allows. We apologise to validators and delegators for the short notice: more details will be shared after the upgrade.

## What v10 brings

v10 moves Chihuahua to the current Cosmos stack:

| Component | v9 | v10 |
|---|---|---|
| Cosmos SDK | v0.50 | v0.54 |
| CometBFT | v0.38 | v0.39 |
| CosmWasm (wasmd / wasmvm) | v0.53 / v2.2 | v0.70 / v3.0 |
| IBC (ibc-go) | v8 | v11 |
| Go | 1.23 | 1.26 |

### On-chain burn counter

The fees burned by `x/feeburn` are now counted on chain. The total starts from the figure published on burn.chihuahua.wtf and grows with every transaction:

```bash
chihuahuad q feeburn total-burned
```

REST: `/chihuahua/feeburn/total_burned`.

### CosmWasm 3 and IBC v11

- Contracts run on wasmvm v3. The CosmWasm capabilities go up to `cosmwasm_2_2`, plus `ibc2` for IBC v2.
- ibc-go v11 brings IBC v2 support. IBC denom traces are migrated to the new denom format: `ibc/...` denoms and balances don't change.
- New ante decorators: CosmWasm simulation gas limit, transaction counter, gas register, and the IBC redundant relay check.

### A leaner chain

Modules with no use left on Chihuahua are removed and their state is cleared:

- `alliance` (retired in v9.5.0)
- `capability` and the IBC fee middleware (ICS-29): removed from ibc-go
- `crisis`, `nft`, `circuit`: unused on Chihuahua
- `params`: every module manages its own parameters

Historical governance proposals that used them can still be queried.

### Maintained by Chihuahua

- `x/liquidity`, previously an external dependency, now lives in the Chihuahua repository.
- `x/group` stays under Apache-2.0: Chihuahua keeps its own copy, and the existing groups keep working unchanged.
- `x/ibc-hooks`, ported to the new store.
- And a new command: `chihuahuad bark`.

## For integrators and contract developers

- The IBC transfer query `DenomTrace` no longer exists in ibc-go: use `Denom` (`/ibc.applications.transfer.v1.Query/Denom`). Contracts using the `DenomTrace` stargate query must switch to `Denom`.
- The REST and gRPC endpoints of the removed modules are gone.

## For validators

- Remove `--x-crisis-skip-assert-invariants` from your start command, if present: v10 no longer accepts it.
- `app.toml` and `config.toml` from v9 keep working.
- The first calls to each contract after the upgrade are slower while wasmvm v3 recompiles it. The old `*-wasmer7` cache can be deleted once the node runs v10.

The upgrade proposal carries the release binaries (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) with their sha256. With cosmovisor v1.7, set in the service environment:

```ini
Environment="DAEMON_ALLOW_DOWNLOAD_BINARIES=true"
Environment="DAEMON_RESTART_AFTER_UPGRADE=true"
Environment="DAEMON_SHUTDOWN_GRACE=30s"
```

Keep `node` in `~/.chihuahuad/config/client.toml` pointed at your node's RPC. With the Huahua Node Manager: `huahua-node upgrade` once the proposal has passed.

Upgrade notes: https://github.com/ChihuahuaChain/chihuahua/blob/main/mainnet/UPGRADES/v10.0.0/README.md

proposals.title: Chihuahua v9.5.0: retire the Alliance module (intermediate upgrade before v10)
proposals.summary:
**Upgrade height: 25571500**, expected around 2026-10-02 12:37 UTC ([countdown](https://explorer.chihuahua.wtf/block/25571500)).

**v9.5.0 is an intermediate upgrade.** It prepares the chain for **v10**, which follows a few days later: Cosmos SDK v0.54, IBC v11, CosmWasm 3.

## What changes

### Alliance retired

Following proposal #99, v9.5.0 retires the Alliance module, which has been inactive since the Migaloo/White Whale project wound down.

- The HUAHUA held by the module is reintroduced into the ecosystem.
- The staked ampGASH and the rewards left unclaimed in the module are burned: they no longer have any use or value.

The module is left empty, and v10 removes it for good.

### Bug fixes

- Stakedrops: fixed the start and end block checks, and the missing payout for the first block.
- Event attributes: `fee_payer` now reports the bech32 address; tokenfactory mint and burn events report the correct address.
- `chihuahuad export` works again.

## Upgrade with cosmovisor (automatic)

The upgrade proposal carries the release binaries (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) with their sha256. With cosmovisor v1.7, set in the service environment:

```ini
Environment="DAEMON_ALLOW_DOWNLOAD_BINARIES=true"
Environment="DAEMON_RESTART_AFTER_UPGRADE=true"
Environment="DAEMON_SHUTDOWN_GRACE=30s"
```

- `DAEMON_ALLOW_DOWNLOAD_BINARIES`: cosmovisor downloads the binary from the proposal and verifies its sha256.
- `DAEMON_SHUTDOWN_GRACE`: cosmovisor stops the old binary cleanly before starting the new one. Without it the old process is killed and the new one can fail to open the database.

Keep `node` in `~/.chihuahuad/config/client.toml` pointed at your node's RPC (`tcp://localhost:26657`, or your RPC port): cosmovisor checks the height through it before switching binaries.

Upgrade notes: https://github.com/ChihuahuaChain/chihuahua/blob/main/mainnet/UPGRADES/v9.5.0/README.md

proposals.title: Sunsetting the ampGASH Alliance: first step of the Chihuahua v10 rebuild
proposals.summary:
## TL;DR

This proposal sets the reward weight and the take rate of the ampGASH Alliance to zero. It is the first step of a full rebuild of the Chihuahua chain, and the Alliance module does not come with us to the new stack.

If you have ampGASH staked in the Alliance: your tokens are safe, nothing is taken from you, and you can unstake them at any time. After this proposal passes they simply stop earning HUAHUA rewards.

## Why now

Chihuahua is still running on Cosmos SDK v0.50. The ecosystem has moved on: SDK v0.54, IBC v11, CosmWasm 3 and CometBFT 0.39 are out, and v0.55 is next. We are preparing the biggest upgrade in the history of the chain to bring everything up to date in one go:

- latest Cosmos SDK, IBC and CosmWasm, with better performance and a much lighter codebase
- removal of old modules that nobody uses anymore (legacy params, IBC fee middleware, capability, Alliance)
- a cleaner and safer fee burn and tokenfactory, with proper test coverage this time
- the groundwork for what comes after: validator key rotation, parallel execution, and new features we will share soon

There are two reasons to close the Alliance, and either one would be enough.

The first is the asset itself. White Whale, the team behind the ecosystem ampGASH comes from, has shut down. ampGASH is no longer developed or supported, and it has been sitting idle in our Alliance for a long time: no Alliance staker has claimed rewards or moved their position in months. Today the chain pays 3% of all staking rewards to an asset that has no project behind it anymore, and that money comes out of the pockets of native HUAHUA stakers.

Keeping it is not just useless, it is a risk. The Alliance turns ampGASH into real HUAHUA voting power on our validators, roughly 9.5% of all bonded stake today. An abandoned asset has nobody watching its contracts, its liquidity or the IBC path it travels on. If anything goes wrong on that side, the damage lands on Chihuahua's staking and consensus, and there is no team left on the other end to fix it.

The second is the software. The Alliance module is maintained by Terra and it stopped at SDK v0.50. There is no version that works with the new stack, so keeping it would mean freezing Chihuahua in the past. We would rather move forward.

## What changes on chain

- ampGASH reward weight: 3% -> 0%
- ampGASH take rate: -> 0%, so staked ampGASH is no longer reduced while it waits to be withdrawn
- the virtual HUAHUA stake that the Alliance adds to validators is removed at the next rebalance. Validators will see their voting power adjust accordingly; relative positions between validators may change slightly
- the 3% of staking rewards that went to Alliance stakers goes back to native HUAHUA stakers

Alliance delegations stay in place and can be undelegated normally. Any ampGASH still in the module at the time of the v10 upgrade will be returned to its owner automatically as part of the upgrade.

## What we ask

If you stake ampGASH on Chihuahua, please unstake over the coming weeks. If you are a validator, get ready: the upgrade plan and the testnet schedule will follow in a separate proposal.

Thanks to everyone who staked ampGASH with us over the past two years. The Alliance made sense when it started; with White Whale gone, it no longer does.

Woof.
